Ui.Script:
-- The continent map's size in pixels — a published pair, because scaling a node's -- normalised position onto the map needs them and so does anything that wants to put its own -- marker there. The values are the specification's (ref TaxiFrame.lua:2-3): a measurement of -- the shipped map art. TAXI_MAP_WIDTH = 316 TAXI_MAP_HEIGHT = 352
-- The static node-button pool's size — see deviation 1 above. BENILLA_TAXI_MAX_NODES = 50
-- What each node state draws (ref TaxiFrame.lua:7-16): CURRENT green, REACHABLE white, -- DISTANT yellow — all three art files verified present in the MPQ. Published as a table of -- `{ file = }` keyed by the state string `TaxiNodeGetType` answers, which is both the shape -- the node paint below reads and the shape an addon adding a state of its own writes. TaxiButtonTypes = { CURRENT = { file = "Interface\\TaxiFrame\\UI-Taxi-Icon-Green" }, REACHABLE = { file = "Interface\\TaxiFrame\\UI-Taxi-Icon-White" }, DISTANT = { file = "Interface\\TaxiFrame\\UI-Taxi-Icon-Yellow" }, }
-- The two strings this window shows, byte-exact from the 1.12 enUS GlobalStrings -- (interface.MPQ `GlobalStrings.lua`, line-cited) — user-visible text, so its bytes are the -- spec, not our expression. `TEXT(x)` (ref l.121) is the real client's build-time no-op -- localization macro, so every `TEXT(FOO)` resolves to the bare `FOO` global -- (CharacterFrame.xml's own convention); with no engine `TEXT` global at all, and nothing -- outside this window reading either string, they are plain locals here instead. local TAXINODEYOUAREHERE = "You are here" -- GlobalStrings.lua:4232 -- GlobalStrings.lua:1864 — the reference's own byte, including its curly apostrophe -- (U+2019, "don\226\128\153t"), not a straight one. local ERR_TAXINOPATHS = "You don\226\128\153t know any flight locations connected to this one."
function TaxiFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this -- The "npc" portrait token (decision 0421): the open taxi session's flight master -- bakes into the ring, resolved exactly like Gossip/Merchant/Trainer's own OnLoad. SetPortraitTexture(getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Portrait"), "npc") frame:RegisterEvent("TAXIMAP_OPENED") frame:RegisterEvent("TAXIMAP_CLOSED") end
-- Deviation 2 above: the flight master's name rides TAXIMAP_OPENED's arg1 (the app -- resolves it through the NameCache) rather than a live UnitName("npc") read. function BenillaTaxiFrame_SetTitle(name) getglobal("TaxiNameText"):SetText(name or "") end
-- Paint the node buttons (ref l.44-63): every pool slot up to the pushed node count takes -- that node's state icon and its pushed position, and the rest of the pool hides. Positions -- arrive normalised 0..1 from the map's BOTTOMLEFT, which is what the map size above scales. local function PaintNodes() local pushed = NumTaxiNodes() for index = 1, BENILLA_TAXI_MAX_NODES do local button = getglobal("TaxiButton" .. index) local state = TaxiNodeGetType(index) if index <= pushed and state ~= "NONE" then local x, y = TaxiNodePosition(button:GetID()) button:ClearAllPoints() button:SetPoint("CENTER", "TaxiMap", "BOTTOMLEFT", x * TAXI_MAP_WIDTH, y * TAXI_MAP_HEIGHT) button:SetNormalTexture(TaxiButtonTypes[state].file) button:Show() else button:Hide() end end end
-- Opening and closing the window (ref TaxiFrame.lua:24-80). Opening repaints everything from -- the pushed snapshot and then asks the panel manager for a slot; if it will not give one, -- the session is closed again rather than left running behind a window nobody can see. function TaxiFrame_OnEvent(event) local frame = this if event == "TAXIMAP_OPENED" then BenillaTaxiFrame_SetTitle(arg1) -- Reset the map's sampling, then hand the region to the app's continent-art pick. TaxiMap:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0, 1) SetTaxiMap(TaxiMap) PaintNodes() ShowUIPanel(frame) if not frame:IsVisible() then CloseTaxiMap() end return end if event == "TAXIMAP_CLOSED" then HideUIPanel(frame) return end end
-- ── The route-line pool ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- A flight path draws as a chain of straight segments, one texture per segment. Those -- textures are a pool that grows to the longest chain ever asked for and is never shrunk: -- `NUM_TAXI_ROUTES` is how many exist and `TaxiRoute<n>` is each one's global name — both -- published, since the count is a global the specification exports and the names are what -- `getglobal` finds. Unlike the node buttons, this half really is created on demand: plain -- region creation carries no template, so deviation 1's CreateFrame wall never applies. NUM_TAXI_ROUTES = 0
-- Grow the pool to hold at least `n` lines; answer what it holds. local function GrowRoutePool(n) while NUM_TAXI_ROUTES < n do NUM_TAXI_ROUTES = NUM_TAXI_ROUTES + 1 local line = TaxiRouteMap:CreateTexture("TaxiRoute" .. NUM_TAXI_ROUTES, "BACKGROUND") line:SetTexture("Interface\\TaxiFrame\\UI-Taxi-Line") end return NUM_TAXI_ROUTES end
-- Draw one line per `{ node, hop }` in `segments`, and hide whatever the pool holds beyond -- them. Each hop's endpoints arrive normalised on the map, so they scale by the canvas the -- lines live on. 32 is the specified line thickness (ref l.114/153), in those same pixels. local function PaintRoutes(segments) local count = table.getn(segments) local pool = GrowRoutePool(count) local w = TaxiRouteMap:GetWidth() local h = TaxiRouteMap:GetHeight() for i = 1, pool do local line = getglobal("TaxiRoute" .. i) if i <= count then local node, hop = segments[i][1], segments[i][2] DrawRouteLine(line, "TaxiRouteMap", TaxiGetSrcX(node, hop) * w, TaxiGetSrcY(node, hop) * h, TaxiGetDestX(node, hop) * w, TaxiGetDestY(node, hop) * h, 32) line:Show() else line:Hide() end end end
-- The tooltip, and the route, for the node under the cursor (ref TaxiFrame.lua:82-126). A -- reachable node prices the flight and draws every hop of it; the node we are standing on -- says so and draws the whole neighbourhood instead. -- -- `this:GetID()` in the fare read is the SAME button as the `button` parameter — the engine -- binds the shared `this` global to the invoking frame before OnEnter runs (decision 0068's -- event-dispatch convention), exactly like the real client, so the two reads agree. function TaxiNodeOnButtonEnter(button) local index = button:GetID() GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:AddLine(TaxiNodeName(index), "", 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
local state = TaxiNodeGetType(index) if state == "REACHABLE" then SetTooltipMoney(GameTooltip, TaxiNodeCost(this:GetID())) TaxiNodeSetCurrent(index) local hops = { } for hop = 1, GetNumRoutes(index) do hops[hop] = { index, hop } end PaintRoutes(hops) elseif state == "CURRENT" then GameTooltip:AddLine(TAXINODEYOUAREHERE, "", 0.5, 1.0, 0.5) DrawOneHopLines() end
GameTooltip:Show() end
-- Every flight path within one hop of where we stand (ref TaxiFrame.lua:129-165) — what the -- map shows the moment it opens, before anything is hovered. A node exactly one segment away -- is one this flight master can send us to directly. function DrawOneHopLines() local hops = { } for node = 1, NumTaxiNodes() do if GetNumRoutes(node) == 1 then table.insert(hops, { node, 1 }) end end PaintRoutes(hops)
-- A flight point with nothing one hop away is a dead end: say so, and take the window -- back down rather than leave an empty map up. if table.getn(hops) == 0 then UIErrorsFrame:AddMessage(ERR_TAXINOPATHS, 1.0, 0.1, 0.1) HideUIPanel(TaxiFrame) end end
-- ── Route lines ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- A flight path is one straight line between two map points, drawn as a texture. The -- engine can only place an AXIS-ALIGNED rectangle, so the rotation has to live in the -- texture coordinates instead: SetTexCoord's 8-argument form places each of the four -- source corners independently, which is exactly enough to spin (and shear) the art -- inside its bounding box. The bounding box then has to grow to hold the rotated line. -- -- The geometry — how a rotation angle turns into those four corners and that box — is -- the specification, and it is the reference's (ref TaxiFrame.lua:168-226; the credit -- their copy carries is to Daniel Stephens <iriel@vigilance-committee.org>). Every value -- below is theirs, and the multiplications are grouped the way theirs are so the rounding -- matches; how it is written — the naming, the shear terms hoisted out of both branches, -- the anchoring helper — is ours. The reference derives each corner from the last -- (`BRx = 1 - BLy`, `TRy = BRx`, …); we state each one directly instead, which is the -- same number everywhere but one: the downward branch's top-left U is `-shearU` here -- against their `1 - (1 + shearU)`. MEASURED, both implementations run side by side on -- the real Lua 5.1 over 50k randomised segments plus the degenerate/axis-aligned/reversed -- edges: every anchor identical to the last bit, and every texture coordinate identical -- once narrowed to f32 — which the engine does to all eight on the way in -- (`region::paint`'s `Variadic<f32>`). The lone survivor is the SIGN OF ZERO on an exactly -- vertical downward line, where that corner is -0 here and +0 there: the same coordinate, -- and the same sample. -- -- Engine seam, all three proved by the phase-1 seam test: CreateTexture, SetTexCoord's -- 8-arg form, and SetPoint against a canvas named by string.
-- The reference's two scale globals, value for value. Only the halved one is ever read — -- by the bounding-box extents below, which are half-widths, hence the /2; the whole one -- is a published global that nothing in the reference reads either. 32/30 is unexplained -- there and carried unchanged here — a measurement of the shipped art, not ours to -- re-derive. TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR = 32/30 TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR_2 = TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR / 2
-- Seat `texture` as the box centred on (cx, cy) that reaches `halfW` / `halfH` out along -- each axis, measured from `canvas`'s `relPoint` corner. Both ends always move together, -- so clearing first is what keeps a stale anchor from outliving a move. (The reference -- re-seats the two points without clearing on its degenerate path; a route texture only -- ever holds these two anchors and SetPoint replaces one of the same name, so the box -- that comes out is the same either way.) local function AnchorCenteredBox(texture, canvas, relPoint, cx, cy, halfW, halfH) texture:ClearAllPoints() texture:SetPoint("BOTTOMLEFT", canvas, relPoint, cx - halfW, cy - halfH) texture:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", canvas, relPoint, cx + halfW, cy + halfH) end
-- Draw the segment (sx,sy) -> (ex,ey), `width` thick, into `texture`, placed against -- `canvas` in the coordinate space of its `relPoint` corner (BOTTOMLEFT by default). function DrawRouteLine(texture, canvas, sx, sy, ex, ey, width, relPoint) relPoint = relPoint or "BOTTOMLEFT"
local dx, dy = ex - sx, ey - sy local cx, cy = (sx + ex) / 2, (sy + ey) / 2
-- A segment drawn back-to-front is the same segment: face it rightwards so only the -- two upward/downward cases below have to exist. if dx < 0 then dx, dy = -dx, -dy end
local len = sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy)) if len == 0 then -- Nothing to draw: collapse the quad onto its own midpoint and show no art. texture:SetTexCoord(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) AnchorCenteredBox(texture, canvas, relPoint, cx, cy, 0, 0) return end
-- Sine and cosine of the segment's angle, and the two shear terms every corner is -- built from — one walking the texture's horizontal axis, one its vertical axis. local sinA, cosA = -dy / len, dx / len local sinSq = sinA * sinA local shear = sinA * cosA local shearU = (width / len) * shear local shearV = (len / width) * shear
-- Half the bounding box the rotated line needs, and the four source corners that lay -- the art across it. Upward and downward are the same algebra mirrored: the four -- quantities are the same, and which corner each lands on is what flips. local halfW, halfH local blU, blV, tlU, tlV, trU, trV, brU, brV if dy >= 0 then halfW = ((len * cosA) - (width * sinA)) * TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR_2 halfH = ((width * cosA) - (len * sinA)) * TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR_2 blU, blV = shearU, sinSq tlU, tlV = sinSq, 1 - shearV trU, trV = 1 - shearU, 1 - sinSq brU, brV = 1 - sinSq, shearV else halfW = ((len * cosA) + (width * sinA)) * TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR_2 halfH = ((width * cosA) + (len * sinA)) * TAXIROUTE_LINEFACTOR_2 blU, blV = sinSq, -shearV tlU, tlV = -shearU, 1 - sinSq trU, trV = 1 - sinSq, 1 + shearV brU, brV = 1 + shearU, sinSq end
-- SetTexCoord's corner order is top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right. texture:SetTexCoord(tlU, tlV, blU, blV, trU, trV, brU, brV) AnchorCenteredBox(texture, canvas, relPoint, cx, cy, halfW, halfH) end
-- Appearing and disappearing. The sounds are the MainMenu pair, not the CharacterInfo pair -- Merchant/Trainer use — the specification genuinely names a different one for this window -- (ref l.162-169). Showing also draws the neighbourhood straight away, so an untouched map -- is not blank; hiding ends the session, which is what fires TAXIMAP_CLOSED back at us. function BenillaTaxiFrame_OnShow() PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen") DrawOneHopLines() end
function BenillaTaxiFrame_OnHide() CloseTaxiMap() PlaySound("igMainMenuClose") end
function BenillaTaxiCloseButton_OnClick() -- vanilla's client-side close sends no packet; the app clears TaxiState on this -- intent (which fires TAXIMAP_CLOSED), and we hide immediately so there's no lag. CloseTaxiMap() HideUIPanel(TaxiFrame) end
